Meet Frank Farry
Frank Farry was elected to the Senate of Pennsylvania in November 2022 to represent the 6th Senate District after serving in the House of Representatives for seven terms. Part of his advocacy focuses on the first responder community, ensuring a quality education, and protecting our taxpayers. A lifelong resident of Bucks County, Farry has been serving his community his entire career.  He has been the chief of Langhorne-Middletown Fire Company since 2001, and a member of the organization for over three decades.

title: HR 212 Report
raw_text:
Choice Should be Paramount in Services Provided to Individuals with Disabilities
﻿
I held a press conference to announce the findings from the Joint State Government Commission report mandated from
House Resolution 212
– which I authored while serving in the House of Representatives.  The report reviewed individuals with disabilities and the services provided by the Office of Developmental Programs (ODP); including work opportunities and living arrangements. View the report
here
.
The press conference was held at Associated Production Services (APS), a packaging company that is employed predominately by individuals with disabilities.  Currently, ODP in their rate setting penalizes operations like APS because there is not a community element. However, we heard from many of the working individuals along with their families and happily working at APS in a clean, safe, and structured environment with their peers is their community.
Learn More
Watch what the workers of APS and their families had to say:
The Denucci Family
Gail Thibodeau and son Matt, APS consumer
In 2017, we held a rally at the Capitol with workers from APS and like workplaces, their families, and service providers advocating for “My Work. My Choice.”  I cannot believe we are still talking about this today.  One astounding issue is that to participate in a work program like APS, you need to be found ineligible for other programs and is considered a setting of last resort.  That doesn’t sound like choice. That sounds like these individuals are being forced in a setting they may not want to be in.
The report reaffirms that choice should be paramount in the services provided by the Office of Developmental Programs (ODP).  The number one recommendation in the report is “promote freedom of choice.”  I am going to use this report as the blueprint to continue to advocate for programs like APS to stay open and ensure individuals with disabilities are treated fairly by having the freedom to choose where they live and work.
Learn More

ai_summary.summary: A Pennsylvania legislator held a press conference to present findings from a state government commission report on disability services, which was required by a resolution the legislator had previously authored. The report examined work and living options for people with disabilities served by the Office of Developmental Programs (ODP) and found that current ODP policies limit choices for individuals, including penalizing sheltered workshop-style employers like Associated Production Services. The legislator stated they plan to use the report to advocate for policy changes that expand freedom of choice in work and housing for people with disabilities.

Neshaminy Baseball—2026 PIAA Class 6A Baseball State Champions
I was incredibly proud to welcome the Neshaminy High School Baseball Team to the Capitol on Tuesday to celebrate and recognize their historic state championship victory.
It was an honor to welcome the players and coaches to the Senate floor and present them with a Pennsylvania Senate citation recognizing this incredible accomplishment. Several family members joined us for the special day, and the team was also recognized on the House floor by Reps. Hogan and Prokopiak.
In their first-ever state championship appearance on June 11 in State College, Neshaminy defeated Butler 7-3 to capture the state title.
I am always proud to welcome students from across our district to the Capitol, but this visit was especially special as I had the opportunity to celebrate my alma mater’s historic achievement. Congratulations to the players, coaches, families, and the entire Neshaminy community on an unforgettable season.
The African American Museum of Bucks County is Now Open
I am pictured here with Sheila Spencer Taylor and her brother, Harvey Spencer Jr., children of the late Harvey Spencer, one of the local residents who first envisioned an African American Museum in Bucks County. Harvey Spencer, Millard Mitchell, and Linda and Alonzo Salley are all commemorated in the museum in recognition of their vision, dedication, and efforts to make this museum a reality.
It was an absolute pleasure to attend the grand opening of the African American Museum of Bucks County this past Friday.
Seeing Linda Salley’s dream and vision become a reality was truly special. Before her passing, Linda and members of the board graciously gave me, Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick and PA State Rep. Joe Hogan a tour of the space and shared what they envisioned for each room. While their descriptions were inspiring, they could not fully capture what I saw on Friday. The finished museum is filled with heart, creativity, and so much history.
This incredible achievement is a testament to the dedication and hard work of the board, volunteers, donors, and everyone who worked tirelessly to bring this vision to life. I was honored to help secure $250,000 in state funding to support the museum in its early stages and am grateful to have played a small role in making this dream a reality.
Linda’s legacy will live on through this museum, ensuring that the stories, contributions, and history of African Americans in Bucks County are preserved and shared for generations to come. Congratulations to everyone who made this day possible.
Visit the
African American Museum of Bucks County’s website
for their hours and to learn more.
Senate Votes to Cut Taxes and Put PA Families First
The Senate approved legislation to dramatically decrease costs for Pennsylvania families by cutting taxes on electric bills and school supplies, strengthening the state’s Educational Improvement Tax Credit (EITC) program and eliminating the current sales tax exemption for data centers.
Making up the largest tax cut in Pennsylvania history, the proposal would eliminate the gross receipts tax on electric bills and require utility companies to pass the reduction on to consumers, saving ratepayers more than $1.7 billion over the first year. It would also implement a two-week sales tax holiday in August for school supplies, such as book bags, crayons, textbooks and tablets.
The highly successful EITC program, which provides scholarships to help families send children to schools that best meet student needs, would receive an additional $25 million under the legislation, bringing the total to $705 million. EITC scholarships remain one of our top priorities for empowering Pennsylvania parents.
House Bill 1667
, as amended by the Senate, also eliminates a long-standing, special sales tax exemption for data centers in the Commonwealth. Data centers would once again be required to pay their fair share of the sales tax when purchasing mechanical equipment, cooling systems, software programs, network infrastructure, security systems, and other equipment necessary for operations.
Reducing the Backlog in PA Rape Kit Testing
For years, Pennsylvania has worked to reduce the backlog of untested rape kits and to ensure survivors of sexual assault are treated with the urgency and dignity they deserve.

The PFC George Raymond Huntzinger Memorial Bridge (Brownsville Rd.) is Now Open
I am pleased to announce the Brownsville Road Bridge over Neshaminy Creek connecting Middletown and Lower Southampton townships reopened five months ahead of schedule and a $1 million less cost to taxpayers.
Prior to the reopening this past Thursday, I joined Rep. Hogan, Matt Allen, Bucks County Veterans Affairs, Ed Preston, chairman PA Vietnam Veterans Memorial Fund, Din Abazi, P.E., District Executive PennDOT, Kevin Loftus, President & CEO, Loftus Construction, local veterans and community members for a rededication ceremony in honor of PFC George Raymond Huntzinger, who gave his life during the Vietnam War. The bridge was originally dedicated in August 2023 before PennDOT began construction to replace the bridge in spring 2025.
Huntzinger, a Langhorne resident, began his tour of duty with the US army on September 11, 1969, and less than two months later on October 29th he tragically lost his life on October while dismantling a landmine in Vietnam. PFC Huntzinger will forever be remembered and honored in our community.
Note: Drone photo supplied by Pennsylvania Department of Transportation (PennDOT)
You can view the full ceremony here

Dax’s 6th Birthday
I was grateful to attend Dax’s Day to celebrate and honor Dax Babcock’s 6th Birthday.
After the Babcock family lost Dax at age 2 in a tragic accident, they created the
Dax Pact
to honor his memory and engage others to live big and love hard just like Dax.
Their foundation is doing remarkable work in Dax’s memory by investing in public parks, donating toy cars and trucks to kids in need, and providing annual scholarships to local daycares and camps.
2026 Woods Services Humanitarian Award
I was proud to honor Kimberly Permar, Executive Director of Bucks County Health Improvement Partnership (BCHIP), with a Pennsylvania Senate citation for being named the 2026 Woods Humanitarian at Woods System of Care Run earlier this month.
Kim’s advocacy on behalf of Woods System of Care projects has increased access to mental health services and attainable housing across Bucks County. This award is a testament to her dedication as she truly exemplifies the spirit of community.
Kimberly and I are pictured here with Woods System of Care President and CEO Tine Hansen-Turton and Woods System of Care Senior Executive VP/Chief Legal and Governance Officer Simon Kimmelman.
BAPS Charities Spirit of Service Walk/Runs
I was proud to join two BAPS Charities Spirit of Service Walk-Runs during the last weekend of May.
The first event was held at Falls Township Community Park supporting the Middletown Community Foundation. The next morning, Lions Pride Park in Warrington hosted the event benefiting the Warrington Township Police Department Shop with a Cop program.
BAPS Charities does an incredible job bringing people together through service and support for local communities. Thank you to everyone who walked, ran, volunteered, and contributed to these great causes.
Save The Date for Our Senior Expo
Our annual Senior Expo will be held on September 17 from 10am to 1pm at Northampton Valley Country Club. There will be exhibitors from state, federal, county, and local agencies offering information on various programs available to assist seniors. There will also be health screenings, senior SEPTA key card processing station, a prescription take-back on site, and much more.

Neshaminy Baseball Team are State Champions
Neshaminy High School defeated Butler High School 7-3 last night to capture the school’s first-ever PIAA Class 6A State Baseball Championship. As a proud Neshaminy graduate, it was incredibly meaningful to be at Penn State University to watch history unfold and celebrate this remarkable achievement alongside students, families, alumni, and community members.
The team led by Coach Dan Toner, demonstrated tremendous talent, resilience, and heart throughout an unforgettable season. They represented their school community with class and earned every bit of this championship.
What makes this victory even more special is that 14 members of this team will graduate tomorrow, with many continuing their academic and athletic careers at the collegiate level. To end their high school careers by bringing home the first ever state baseball championship in school history is something they, their families, and our entire community will never forget.
Phoenix Sports Club Celebrates 100 Years
It was great to join Phoenix Sports Club, the first German sports club of its kind in our region, Congressman Fitzpatrick, Rep. Hogan and many community members, as they celebrated 100 years of community, culture and athletics.
I was proud to present a Pennsylvania Senate citation for this incredible milestone and a century of making a difference in our community.
Recognizing Local Eagle Scout in Harrisburg
I was proud to welcome recent William Tennent High School graduate Connor Cumiskey and his family to the Senate floor this week. Connor is a member of Boy Scout Troop 139 and earned his Eagle Scout rank this past December.
In attaining his Eagle Scout, Connor helped to beautify and clean up gardens at Good Shepherd Lutheran Church in Southampton and earned 43 merit badges and 4 eagle palms while holding the positions of patrol leader and troop historian.
Only attained by a small percentage of all Scouts, this monumental achievement represents the great sacrifice and tremendous efforts that were made by this young leader. Congratulations to Connor and I wish him the best of luck and success in his future.
Strengthening Research and Development in Pennsylvania
My legislation to strengthen Pennsylvania’s position as a leader in research and development was approved by the Senate Institutional Sustainability and Innovation Committee this week.
Senate Bill 792
would significantly expand Pennsylvania’s Research and Development Tax Credit Program by doubling the annual statewide cap from $60 million to $120 million and increasing the small-business allocation from $12 million to $24 million. The legislation also allows unused credits to be reallocated between small-business and large-business pools, ensuring the full value of available credits can be utilized each year.
These improvements make our tax credit program more competitive and accessible, particularly for startups and growing businesses that are often at the forefront of innovation. By encouraging companies to invest in research here in Pennsylvania, we can help create new opportunities for workers and strengthen our economy for years to come.
Most importantly, these funds help support the search for the next cure, breakthrough treatment, or life-changing medical device that can bring hope and improve the lives of those facing disease, injury, and other health challenges.
Senate Passes Bill to Fight Human Trafficking
Legislation to give investigators and prosecutors new tools to fight human trafficking in Pennsylvania was passed by the Senate.
Senate Bill 45
will help local law enforcement agencies and the state attorney general investigate and prosecute human trafficking by increasing penalties for several related crimes, including promoting prostitution, promoting prostitution of a minor, exploiting prostitutes and patronizing prostitutes.
The bill also consolidates crimes related to human trafficking within the Crimes Code, giving the attorney general concurrent jurisdiction so these crimes, which are frequently the basis for large-scale human trafficking organizations, can be prosecuted more effectively.
It now moves to the House of Representatives for consideration. If you believe you may have information about a trafficking situation, call the National Human Trafficking Hotline at 888-373-7888.
Read more about our latest action to combat human trafficking here
.

Celebrating 250 Years of American Freedom
250 years ago – on July 4, 1776 – our nation’s founders gathered in Philadelphia and signed the
Declaration of Independence
. President Abraham Lincoln once described the Declaration as “an apple of gold” and said it gave “liberty, not alone to the people of this country, but hope to the world for all future time.”
I hope you have a wonderful Fourth of July weekend with friends and family celebrating the birth of this great nation. If you are looking for a way to celebrate, here are the events happening in the 6

Honoring the Life of Lyle Winters
I was honored to attend the services for Lyle Winters of Parkland Fire Company and present a Senate condolence resolution to his children in recognition of the extraordinary life he lived.
Lyle was a true pioneer in the fire service as one of the first members of Parkland Fire Company, the first full-time paid Fire Marshal for Middletown Township, and the first firefighter in the United States to use the Hurst Tool, better known as the “Jaws of Life.”
He helped shape the future of emergency response. His leadership, innovation, and unwavering commitment to serving others will leave a lasting impact on Parkland, Middletown Township, and surrounding communities.
I had the privilege of knowing Lyle personally, and I know his legacy will continue to inspire generations of firefighters and first responders.
My deepest condolences go out to Lyle’s family and friends, and to his brothers and sisters at Parkland Fire Company. May we always remember and honor a life dedicated to serving others.
Michael Bean Honored for 28 Years Protecting the Community
I was proud to recognize Michael Bean on his retirement from Newtown Fire-Rescue and honor his twenty-eight years of dedicated service to our community.
Michael has served Newtown Fire-Rescue as a firefighter, Emergency Medical Technician, field officer and Shift Supervisor. His passion for the fire service extends beyond his career, as he also serves as the volunteer Fire Chief of Warrington Fire Company, a role he will continue in retirement.
Thank you to Michael for his decades of dedication, sacrifice, and leadership. Congratulations on an outstanding career and continued service to the community.

Celebrating the Grand Opening of Playa Raya
I was honored to join First Lady Lori Shapiro, Secretary of Transportation Mike Carrol, Rabbi Yudy Shemtov and his dedicated team, Representatives Hogan and Warren, and many members of our community to celebrate Playa Raya’s grand opening.
The celebration marked the opening of an incredible new facility featuring a zero-entry swimming pool and splash pad. Designed specifically for individuals with special needs and their families, Playa Raya is on the site of the former Breezy Point Swim Club in Northampton Township.
The pool and splash pad is the first phase of the project with future phases including walking trails, fitness stations, and accessible playgrounds, with plans to eventually add pickleball courts as well as equestrian facilities.
Rep. Marcell, Rep. Hogan and I were proud to secure $500,000 in state funding to help make the vision of Playa Raya a reality. Playa Raya will provide countless families with an inclusive, welcoming place to gather, play, and create lasting memories.
Visit their website to learn more about Playa Raya

Pinning Ceremony for Lt. Colonel Horne
It was an honor to attend the pinning ceremony celebrating Zachary Horne’s promotion to Lieutenant Colonel on July 4 at his family’s restaurant, The Irish Horne in Richboro.
A proud Council Rock South graduate, Lt. Colonel Horne has served our nation for the past 17 years, including deployments to Afghanistan and assignments in Germany.
Thank you to Lt. Colonel Horne for his service, sacrifice, and unwavering dedication to our nation. It was a privilege to celebrate this special milestone with you, your family, and Rep. Kristin Marcell.
Celebrating a Remarkable Career in Catholic Education
Congratulations to Jessica McDonald on her retirement after 57 years of dedicated service to Catholic education. I was pleased to join the celebration and present her with a Pennsylvania Senate citation recognizing this incredible milestone.
Since beginning her teaching career in 1968, Mrs. McDonald has inspired generations of students with her kindness, compassion, and unwavering commitment to learning. She devoted the past 35 years to teaching third grade at St. Bede the Venerable School, now St. Katharine Drexel Catholic School, while also faithfully serving her parish and volunteering her time to support students beyond the classroom.
I thank Mrs. McDonald for her extraordinary commitment to education and wish her many happy years of retirement filled with family, travel, and treasured memories with her grandchildren.
Senate Passes Bill to Bring Life-saving Treatments to Market More Quickly
The Senate approved legislation to help get new life-saving treatments and devices to market more quickly while preserving safety standards. The bill was sent to the House of Representatives for consideration.
Under current law, a pharmaceutical or medical device manufacturer must first complete a lengthy federal process before it can even begin the state licensure process in Pennsylvania.
Senate Bill 1206
allows companies to gain temporary approval under Pennsylvania’s virtual manufacturers’ law, so that once federal approval is granted, these companies can quickly move forward without having to clear additional administrative roadblocks.
As chair of the Institutional Sustainability and Innovation Committee, I was proud to co-sponsor this important legislation and help advance it by passing it out of committee in June.
Read more about Senate Bill 1206 here
.
Strengthening Medical Imaging Standards
Medical imaging – such as MRIs or x-rays – are essential to diagnosing and treating a wide range of medical conditions and rely on radiation to do so. Performed incorrectly, these tests can cause serious harm to patients.
Yet, Pennsylvania is one of only four states that do not have a licensure or certification framework for these professionals. The Senate approved
Senate Bill 1334
to create a statewide licensing structure for professionals who perform medical imaging and radiation therapy procedures.
The bill doesn’t require additional schooling or place unnecessary burdens on qualified professionals. It was sent to the House of Representatives for consideration.
Read more about Senate Bill 1334 here
.

The Property Tax/Rent Rebate Program provides rebates on property taxes or rent paid for the previous year by income-eligible seniors and people with disabilities. The deadline to apply has been extended to Dec. 31, 2026.

PFC George Raymond Huntzinger Memorial Bridge Rededication
On June 18, the Brownsville Road Bridge over Neshaminy Creek connecting Middletown and Lower Southampton townships reopened five months ahead of schedule and a $1 million less cost to taxpayers.
Prior to the reopening, I joined Rep. Hogan, Matt Allen, Bucks County Veterans Affairs, Ed Preston, Chairman PA Vietnam Veterans Memorial Fund, Din Abazi, P.E., District Executive PennDOT, Kevin Loftus, President & CEO, Loftus Construction, local veterans and community members for a rededication ceremony in honor of PFC George Raymond Huntzinger, a fallen solder in the Vietnam War. The bridge was originally dedicated in August 2023 before PennDOT began construction to replace the bridge in spring 2025.
Huntzinger, a Langhorne resident, began his tour of duty with the US army on September 11, 1969, and less than two months later on October 29
th
he tragically lost his life on October while dismantling a landmine in Vietnam. PFC Huntzinger will forever be remembered and honored in our community.

PA Guard Military Family Education Program
As students begin preparing for the fall semester, Pennsylvania National Guard members are reminded their families could be eligible for assistance to offset the cost of higher education.
The Military Family Education Program is for Guard members who completed an initial service obligation on or after July 1, 2019, and are eligible to re-enlist in the PA National Guard for a period of six years.
The grants can be used for a degree-granting or certificate-granting curriculum, course of study, or training program required for entrance into a specific career at an approved Pennsylvania institution of higher learning.
Read more details and find applications here

Beware of the “Veterans Savings Program” Postcard Scam
Veterans and their spouses are being targeted by a new postcard scam advertising a fraudulent “Veterans Saving Program.” The mailer claims eligibility for an extra $185 monthly payment and dental benefits, but the program does not exist.
More information about this scam is available here.
Veteran Benefits Assistance
The Pennsylvania Department of Military and Veterans Affairs (DMVA) provides veterans and their beneficiaries with free and safe assistance when applying for benefits. Seeking free help from the DMVA can help veterans avoid scams and exploitation from people looking to profit from veterans earned benefits.
For more information about pension poaching, click here.
Veteran Burial Benefits
Eligible veterans and their spouses can receive no-cost burial benefits at U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) national cemeteries. These benefits include burial in a VA National Cemetery, headstone or marker with inscription included and gravesite maintenance in perpetuity.
Veterans’ spouses are still eligible for these benefits if they pre-decease the veteran or if the veteran is interred in a non-VA cemetery.
For more information on veteran burial benefits from the VA, click here.
National Parks Military Lifetime Pass
Veterans of the U.S. Armed Forces and members of Gold Star Families are eligible for a free Military Lifetime Pass at national parks, which will admit the passholder and accompanying passengers in a non-commercial vehicle at per vehicle fee areas, or the passholder and up to three additional people over the age of 16 where per person fees are charged.
Passes cover entrance and day-use fees at lands managed by the National Park Service, the Bureau of Land Management, the Bureau of Reclamation, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, the U.S. Forest Service and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers.

New State Budget Protects Taxpayers and Funds Priorities
This past Sunday, my colleagues and I passed the 2026-27 state budget. This budget delivers for Pennsylvanians by making meaningful investments in education, workforce development, and our retirees while continuing to protect taxpayers. I remain committed to protecting taxpayers while working to empower families, create job opportunities, support students, working families and seniors. I’m your voice in Harrisburg that is always putting our community first.
Cost of Living Adjustment for Retired Teachers, Police and Firefighters
The newly enacted state budget includes a cost-of-living (COLA) increase for retired teachers, school district employees and state employees who retired prior to July 2, 2001, as well as certain retired municipal firefighters and police officers.
Many of these employees retired before 2000 at a much lower retirement system than current employees. In addition, they did not receive the pension benefit enhancements under Act 9 of 2001 and have now gone more than 20 years without a COLA.
The COLAs are fully funded through existing interactive gaming tax revenues, ensuring these benefit enhancements have no impact on state, school district or municipal taxes. The legislation directs a portion of those revenues to fund the pension increases and reimburse municipalities for the municipal benefit adjustments, with any remaining funding continuing to support an existing grant program. These men and women dedicated years to serving our communities, and I’m pleased to support this long-overdue increase in their pensions.

Senate Stands with Attorney General, District Attorneys, State Troopers and Police
Second-degree murder is a horrific crime – these are homicides committed while the defendant was also committing another violent felony such as rape, arson, robbery, burglary or kidnapping. Those who commit such an act deserve a punishment that matches.
In March, the Pennsylvania Supreme Court ruled that our current sentencing structure for second-degree murder (life without parole in every case) is unconstitutional. The justices gave the General Assembly 120 days to enact legislation correcting the situation.
The Senate
successfully passed strong bipartisan legislation to address this issue
– twice. Once in June and again in early July. The Senate’s legislation is supported by Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday, Pennsylvania District Attorneys Association, the Pennsylvania State Troopers Association, the Pennsylvania Chiefs of Police Association, and Pennsylvania State Lodge Fraternal Order of Police.
The House refused to take action on this important issue until day 119 of the court-imposed 120 day deadline. Unfortunately, the majority leadership in the House of Representatives refused to allow a full House vote on this bipartisan legislation, instead in committee amended the bill to weaken it thereby taking away the opportunity for the full House of Representatives to vote on the issue. The House added a provision to the bill as amended that could allow more than half of all inmates who have not served their full sentence, including those on death row for killing children or a police officer, to qualify for release from prison under a weakly defined “medical release” program. As the House debated the bill, one side of the aisle seemed focused on relief for convicted murderers while the other focused on not revictimizing the family members whose loved one was murdered. The bill passed with nearly 100% of the vote on party lines.
The majority of the public was unaware of this issue and the deadline that the House failed to meet last week. Myself, and local representatives held a press conference last week to help make the public aware of the issue and most importantly to stand for the murder victim’s family members.
Here is a link to the press conference
. To watch my videos on the issue, you can visit my
Facebook page
.
As a result of the House Majority’s failures over 1,100 convicted murderers will now be able to seek their release including 17 from Bucks County and 545 from Philadelphia.

Pennsylvania Has New Tools to Solve Violent Crimes
Law enforcement agencies will be able to access new tools to boost clearance rates for homicide and other violent crime cases through a new state law.

was enacted with the new state budget. The law establishes a grant program administered by the Pennsylvania Commission on Crime and Delinquency to help police hire and retain detectives and investigators, and upgrade technology used to analyze evidence.

In this Update:
Upcoming Events
Supporting Our First Responders
Updates to U.S. 1 PennDOT Improvement Project
Understanding Digital Threats to Children
Upcoming Events
Home Safety Event
I hope you can join us for a Home Safety Event hosted by Kidde on August 29
th
from 11 am to 1 pm at Middle Bucks Institute of Technology, located at 2740 York Rd.in Jamison.
Attendees will have the opportunity to refresh their fire and carbon monoxide safety knowledge, while enjoying a variety of family-friendly activities. I will be joined by Rep. Marcell and members of the Warwick Fire Department.
The event will feature fire and carbon monoxide safety education tools, a meet and greet with Peppa Pig, a snow cone truck, giveaways, and more. Free smoke detectors will be available to community members who need them.
Learn More about Kidde and their Cause For Alarm Campaign
Senior Expo
We invite seniors and their families of the 6
th
Senatorial District to our annual Senior Expo. The expo is a ‘one stop shop’ opportunity to gather valuable information and meet face to face with people in our area who can assist them with a wide range of services. It will be held on Thursday September 17 from 10 am to 1 pm at Northampton Valley Country Club.
The event will feature exhibitors from state, federal, county, and local agencies offering information on various programs available to assist seniors. There will also be health screenings, senior SEPTA key card processing station, and a prescription take-back on site.
Our staff will be onsite to help with any state-related questions. We hope you can join us for this informative and fun day.
Bensalem Shredding Event
Rep. Tomlinson and I are hosting a Shredding Event on Saturday September 19 from 10 am to noon at Bensalem High School, located at 4319 Hulmeville Ave in Bensalem.
With the cases of identity theft rising at a significant rate, this is a great opportunity to properly dispose of documents containing personal information. Residents of the 6
th
Senatorial district are encouraged to bring documents that contain sensitive information, such as Social Security numbers, medical information, or bank account numbers, to be thoroughly shredded.
Due to high demand, individuals are limited to two file boxes of paper to be shredded. Please do not place your paper in plastic bags as it cannot be shredded. This is an event for residents only, no businesses, please.
Prior to the event, please place all shredding materials and donation items in the trunk of your vehicle.  Once you arrive, stay in your vehicle and staff will assist with removing the materials.
Any questions about our upcoming events, please call our office at 215-638-1784
or visit our website
Supporting Our Local First Responders
Last Tuesday night, I had the opportunity to visit several National Night Out events across the 6th Senatorial District. National Night Out is an annual event that brings police, first responders, and the community together to build stronger relationships and promote public safety. It was great to speak with so many of our local first responders and residents who make our community stronger.
As your state senator, I am proud to bring state funding back to our communities to support our first responders, helping to ease the burden on taxpayers while supporting the vital services our communities rely on. I have helped secure over $700,000 in state funding for our fire and EMS companies across the 6
th
District. It was especially rewarding to see firsthand how these investments are being put to use in our communities.
At the Warminster Township National Night Out, I was proud to present a state funding check to the Warminster Fire Department to support the purchase of new AEDs for their Department. These lifesaving devices will help our firefighters and emergency responders provide critical care when seconds matter.
At the Bensalem National Night Out, I had the opportunity to see the new regional SWAT vehicle that Reps. Marcell, Tomlinson, and Hogan and I helped secure $350,000 in state funding to purchase. The vehicle has been delivered and housed in Bensalem and is expected to enter service soon. It will serve all three Bucks County regional special units and tactical SWAT teams, helping drastically reduce response times

title: News for Veterans – August 2026
raw_text:
News for Veterans - August 2026 - Senator Farry
News for Veterans - August 2026 - Senator Farry
View this email in a browser
In this Update:
State Budget Supports Veterans and Their Families
New Law Connects Families of Deceased Services Members with Support
Honoring Veterans with Visual Impairments with a Capitol Monument
Addressing Veteran Homelessness
VA and Steak ‘N Shake Promote Veterans Benefits
Free Ray-Ban Meta AI Glasses for Blind Veterans
No-Cost TSA Precheck for Eligible Veterans
State Budget Supports Veterans and Their Families
On July 12, we finalized the 2026-27 state budget that included creating and enhancing programs and services aimed at assisting Pennsylvania veterans and their families such as:
Providing a 6.3% increase for tuition assistance to children of honorably discharged veterans who have service-connected disabilities and served during a period of war or armed conflict and children of veterans who die or died in service during a period of war or armed conflict.
Providing a 10.2% increase for the
Amputee and Paralyzed Veterans’ Pension
, which gives eligible veterans a $150 monthly pension.
Establishing the Veterans’ Trust Fund Board within the Pennsylvania Department of Military and Veterans Affairs to increase donations to the Veterans’ Trust Fund and provide for effective management of the fund.
Requiring the Department of Human Services to expand online referral services and information for military veterans and their families for transitional, temporary and permanent housing, job placement and career counseling and other services for veterans returning to civilian life.
New Law Connects Families of Deceased Services Members with Support
In an effort to better connect families with their local veterans affairs office, the General Assembly unanimously passed
Senate Bill 130
, now Act 42 of 2026, which requires funeral directors and cemeteries to provide the family of a deceased serviceperson contact information for the county director of veterans affairs. They must also notify the county director of veterans affairs of the death of a service person within 96 hours of receiving their remains.
Pennsylvania county veterans affairs offices are available to better assist veterans access benefits for which they might be eligible, and
their contact information can be found here
.
Honoring Veterans with Visual Impairments with a Capitol Monument
A Braille Flag monument honoring veterans with visual impairments could be installed at the Pennsylvania Capitol Building under legislation passed by the Senate and sent to the House of Representatives for consideration.
The Braille Flag was created to honor the service of veterans who have been left with life-long visual disabilities. Under
Senate Bill 1303
, the monument would be made of bronze and include the Pledge of Allegiance in Braille.
The display would be sponsored by the Moose Lodge and the American Braille Flag Project, a non-profit organization dedicated to the placement of these flags throughout the country.
Read more about Senate Bill 1303 here
.
Addressing Veteran Homelessness
The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs’
Homeless Aging and Disabled Veterans Initiative
aims to help homeless veterans with chronic, complex health needs secure affordable housing within their communities or transition more easily to any higher levels of care they need. The initiative works to better integrate home and community healthcare, social services and permanent supportive housing.
Veterans experiencing homelessness should visit their local VA Medical Center for assistance. To find a VA Medical Center near you,
visit their website here
. For immediate assistance, contact the National Call Center for Homeless Veterans at (877) 4AID-VET (877-424-3838).
To learn more about VA Homeless Programs, click here.
VA and Steak ‘N Shake Promote Veterans Benefits
VA has teamed up with Steak ‘n Shake to promote VA benefits and services and make it easier for veterans to become owner-operators of Steak ‘n Shake franchises.
As a part of their agreement, Steak ‘n Shake will:
Waive the $10,000 franchise fee for veterans seeking to run their own franchise under its Franchise Partner Program for Veterans.
Promote awareness of VA benefits and healthcare on their website and through in-restaurant signage.
Prioritize hiring veterans and VA beneficiaries, including family, caregivers and survivors for leadership positions across the company.
Find more information here.
Free Ray-Ban Meta AI Glasses for Blind Veterans
Meta is donating
free Ray-Ban Meta AI glasses
to every blind veteran in the U.S.
Veterans can apply after becoming a
Blinded Veterans Association (BVA) member
.
Veteran organizations can apply to receive glasses for the blinded veterans in their communities here.
No-Cost TSA Precheck for Eligible Veterans
The VETS (Veterans Expedited TSA Screening) Safe Travel Act was signed into law, allowing certain veterans to
receive no-cost TSA PreCheck enrollment
. TSA

ai_summary.summary: Senator Farry's August 2026 veterans newsletter summarizes several recent legislative and program developments affecting Pennsylvania veterans, including budget increases for tuition assistance and disability pensions, a new law requiring funeral directors to notify county veterans affairs offices of deceased service members, and a Senate-passed bill to install a Braille Flag monument at the state Capitol. The newsletter also highlights federal and private-sector programs related to veteran homelessness, franchise opportunities, free AI glasses for blind veterans, and no-cost TSA PreCheck.

raw_text:

In this Update:
Join Us for our Home Safety Event
Supporting St. Mary’s Breast Imaging Center
Honoring Three Local Eagle Scouts
Women’s Animal Center Clear the Shelters Adoption Event
School Bus Safety Legislation Awaits House Action
Join Us for our Home Safety Event
I hope you can join us for a Home Safety Event hosted by Kidde on August 29
th
from 11 am to 1 pm at Middle Bucks Institute of Technology, located at 2740 York Rd.in Jamison.
Attendees will have the opportunity to refresh their fire and carbon monoxide safety knowledge, while enjoying a variety of family-friendly activities. I will be joined by Rep. Marcell and members of the Warwick Fire Department.
The event will feature fire and carbon monoxide safety education tools, a meet and greet with Peppa Pig, a snow cone truck, giveaways, and more. Free smoke detectors will be available to community members who need them.
Learn More about Kidde and their Cause For Alarm Campaign
Learn more about our Upcoming Senior Expo and Shredding Event
Supporting St. Mary’s Breast Imaging Center
I am proud to have help secure state funding, along with Rep. Hogan, to support St. Mary Medical Center’s Breast Imaging Center. This investment will enhance women’s medical imaging by improving patient comfort, strengthening staff expertise, and replacing breast ultrasound transducers. The funding will also support on-site clinical training for radiologists and technologists, ensuring the breast biopsy procedures are conducted safely, accurately, and efficiently.
Honoring Three Local Eagle Scouts
I was honored to attend the Court of Honor ceremonies recognizing three local young men who recently achieved the rank of Eagle Scout—the highest advancement rank in the Boy Scouts of America. Only a small percentage of Scouts attain this prestigious rank, making it a tremendous accomplishment that reflects years of dedication, leadership, and service.
I congratulate these outstanding young leaders and commend them for the lasting impact they have made in our community through their Eagle Scout projects:
Noah Kelly – Troop 153, Feasterville
: Completed maintenance at Idlewood trails and installed a trail map entrance.
Dylan Wild, Troop 153, Feasterville
: Reconstructed seventeen benches at Playwicki Farm.
Tyler Everly, Troop 139, Warminster:
Designed and built K-9 training equipment for the Plymouth Township Police Department.
I presented each Scout with a citation from the Senate of Pennsylvania recognizing this outstanding achievement and their many years of service and leadership in our community.
Women’s Animal Center Clear the Shelters Adoption Event
Women’s Animal Center is a participating shelter for the 12th Annual NBCUniversal ‘Clear the Shelters’ nationwide pet adoption event that helps find loving forever homes for surrendered and stray animals. And thanks to the generous financial support of Inspire Federal Credit Union as this year’s Event Partner, adoption fees for cats, dogs and small animals will be FREE for individuals and families adopting from Women’s Animal Center on Saturday, August 29th.
The event will also feature complimentary refreshments, giveaways for adopters and coloring activities for the kids. All shelter pets adopted from Women’s Animal Center are spayed and/or neutered, receive preventative and lifesaving vaccines, and are microchipped which provides a permanent means of identification should a pet become separated from its new family.  Adopters will also receive 10% off in the Veterinary Hospital for their pet’s first annual physical exam.
Those interested in adopting a shelter pet are invited to visit Women’s Animal Center at 3839 Richlieu Road in Bensalem on Saturday, August 29th from 10am-2pm.
To prepare for the day, potential adopters should FIRST visit the Center’s website
adoption page to view photos of adoptable pets and for information about the adoption process and what/who to bring.
School Bus Safety Legislation Awaits House Action
Over the past five years, 25,136 Pennsylvania drivers have been cited for school zone violations, including 8,302 for overtaking or illegally passing a school bus.
The Unified Judicial System of Pennsylvania breaks down the numbers here
.
In September 2025, the Senate unanimously passed
Senate Bill 65
, Enhancing the Safe Transportation of School Children, which would extend the stopping distance requirement from 10 feet to 15 feet before reaching the bus when the red signal lights are flashing and the side stop arm is activated. It also develops a tiered penalty system for a second or subsequent offense. Current law does not penalize repeat offenders.
With the start of a new school year nearly a year later, it still awaits a vote by the full House of Representatives.
Read more about this effort to boost school bus safety here
.

Join Us for our Home Safety Event Tomorrow
I hope you can join us for a Home Safety Event hosted by Kidde tomorrow, August 29
th
from 11 am to 1 pm at Middle Bucks Institute of Technology, located at 2740 York Rd.in Jamison.
Attendees will have the opportunity to refresh their fire and carbon monoxide safety knowledge, while enjoying a variety of family-friendly activities. I will be joined by Rep. Marcell and members of the Warwick Fire Department.
The event will feature fire and carbon monoxide safety education tools, a meet and greet with Peppa Pig, a snow cone truck, giveaways, and more. Free smoke detectors will be available to community members who need them.
Learn More about Kidde and their Cause For Alarm Campaign
Learn more about our Upcoming Senior Expo and Shredding Event
Women’s Animal Center Clear the Shelters Adoption Event is Tomorrow
Women’s Animal Center is a participating shelter for the 12th Annual NBCUniversal ‘Clear the Shelters’ nationwide pet adoption event that helps find loving forever homes for surrendered and stray animals. And thanks to the generous financial support of Inspire Federal Credit Union as this year’s Event Partner, adoption fees for cats, dogs and small animals will be FREE for individuals and families adopting from Women’s Animal Center on Saturday, August 29th.
The event will also feature complimentary refreshments, giveaways for adopters and coloring activities for the kids. Those interested in adopting a shelter pet are invited to visit Women’s Animal Center at 3839 Richlieu Road in Bensalem on Saturday, August 29th from 10am-2pm.  To prepare for the day, potential adopters should FIRST
visit the Center’s website adoption page to view photos of adoptable pets and for information about the adoption process and what/who to bring
.
Supporting Organizations Making a Difference
Earlier this month, I had the opportunity to attend Amazon’s Rise & Recognize event at Bucks County Community College, where local non-profits and organizations across Bucks County were awarded grants to support projects making a positive impact in our community.
I am pictured here with Karen and Michael Babcock from the Dax Pact Foundation, a grant recipient that will use the funding to help support the expansion of three of their signature programs and continue their mission of spreading smiles and joy in the quiet moments of life, creating meaningful experiences while keeping Dax’s spirit alive.
I am also pictured with Jennifer Schultz from Centennial Education Foundation and Kristin Herman from Centennial School District, a grant recipient that will use its funding to expand programming at the Betty Huf Planetarium located at William Tennent High School.
Other notable recipients included Network of Victim Assistance (NOVA), TMA Bucks Foundation, Inc, and Southampton Free Library.
Lower Bucks Chamber of Commerce State of the State
Earlier this week, I attended Lower Bucks Chamber of Commerce’s State of the State. I joined a bipartisan group of Lower Bucks County state officials to provide a legislative update and answer questions on important issues to the business community.
Some of the topics discussed were affordability, early childhood education, and first responder issues.
Helping Families Keep Kids Involved
As a parent, I understand the costs that come with raising a family. Every child should have the opportunity to participate in activities such as sports, music, Scouts, dance or karate—regardless of their family’s financial circumstances.
That’s why I recently introduced legislation to establish a tax credit for parents of eligible school-age children to help offset the growing costs of participation in youth activities. The credit aims to reduce the financial burden of equipment purchases, travel expenses, and participation fees for a wide range of organized activities, including sports, performances, lessons and competitions.
This would make youth activities more affordable for families while helping children build confidence, friendships and valuable life skills.
Treasury Launches New Financial Education Hub
Pennsylvania Treasurer Stacy Garrity announced the launch of the department’s online Financial Education Hub, a one-stop-shop of resources designed to help Pennsylvanians improve their financial literacy and make informed financial decisions.
The new hub brings together state and federal resources covering topics such as budgeting, saving, retirement planning, digital assets and cryptocurrencies. It also includes

Home Safety Event Success
Thank you to everyone who helped make our Home Safety Event a success. We had great day full of learning, community and fun. Rep. Kristin Marcell and I enjoyed having the opportunity to engage with constituents.
A special thank you to Kidde Fire Safety for all their work planning this event and providing our community with valuable fire and carbon monoxide safety tips, and alarm donations.

I am hosting a free Senior Expo on September 17 from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. at the Northampton Valley Country Club, located at 299 Richboro Rd. in Richboro. The event will feature exhibitors from state, federal, county, and local agencies offering information on various programs available to assist seniors.

To help residents guard themselves against identity theft, Rep. Tomlinson and are hosting a free paper shredding event on Saturday, September 19 from 10 am- noon at Bensalem High School, located at 4319 Hulmeville Ave.
Residents of the 6
th
Senate District are encouraged to bring documents that contain sensitive information to be thoroughly shredded. We are also accepting donations of pet food and pet supplies in partnership with Women’s Animal Center.

Breaking New Ground Honoring a Legacy of Service
I was proud to join Woods System of Care and local elected officials last week for the groundbreaking of the Barry R. Sharer Pavilion, honoring a longtime leader whose dedication and service will now have a lasting impact on Woods and the people they support.
This project will provide housing for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities and neurodivergence alongside the broader community, helping create an inclusive community full of opportunity.

We need your help to get
Senate Bill 1441
and
House Bill 2753
moving in Harrisburg. Too often, good legislation can take years to become law. With enough support from families like yours, we can show our fellow lawmakers that Pennsylvania families want and need this tax credit—and help get it passed sooner.
Please take a moment to
sign the petition
and show your support. Feel free to share with family and friends.

Attorney General Dave Sunday announced Pennsylvania and a multistate coalition have reached a settlement with Meta, owner of Instagram and Facebook, assuring the social media giant will implement sweeping changes to age verification, limit children’s time on their platforms and cut kids’ access to harmful content.

Road Dedication in Honor of Captain Walter H. Sigafoos III
Please join Rep. Marcell and I on Friday, Sept. 18, at 10:30 a.m. at Addisville Church, 945 Second Street Pike in Richboro, for the dedication of a portion of Second Street Pike in honor of U.S. Air Force Capt. Walter H. Sigafoos III.
Capt. Sigafoos and his pilot, Lt. Col. Jeffrey C. Lemon, were declared missing in action after a mission over Laos on April 25, 1971, during the Vietnam War.
Connecting with Local Veterans
It was great to connect with local veterans at The Friends of Valor Golf Outing last week. This great community event brings together golfers, sponsors and community members to honor and support local and national heroes.
Proceeds from the outing support programs like Victor Six, founded by Vietnam veteran David Christian, which works to improve the physical and mental well-being of veterans and reduce the risk of suicide in the veteran community.
Travis Manion 9/11 Heroes Run
The
Travis Manion Foundation
(TMF), a non-profit organization is hosting several upcoming 5Ks throughout the U.S. in honor of the 25
th
anniversary of September 11, 2001, including one in Feasterville. It will be held on Sept. 12 at 9 a.m. starting at Russell E Elliot Memorial Park.
Please visit their website for more information
.
The 9/11 Heroes Run 5K welcomes runners, ruckers, and walkers of all ages and fitness levels to honor the heroes of that day and those who stepped up to serve in the wars that followed. These annual events are critical to helping Americans fulfill a promise to never forget and share the significance of that day with future generations.
Veterans Temporary Assistance Program
The Pennsylvania Department of Veterans Affairs (DMVA) administers the Veterans Temporary Assistance (VTA) Program which provides temporary financial assistance up to $1,600 for necessities including food, shelter, fuel and clothing within a 12-month period to eligible veterans and their beneficiaries who reside in Pennsylvania.
To be eligible, veterans must have served in the U.S. Armed Forces, been honorably discharged after a period of active duty other than active duty for training, died in service or suffered a service-connected disability as certified by the U.S. Veterans’ Administration.
The
DMVA website
lists the financial circumstances that qualify veterans for help via the VTA program. Veterans interested in applying for a VTA grant should contact the
County Director of Veterans Affairs
within the county they reside.
New Law Connects Families with VA Burial Benefits
Under a new law,
Act 42 of 2026
, families of a deceased service person being buried or cremated in Pennsylvania after Sept. 18 will receive contact information for their county veterans affairs office from funeral directors and cemeteries. County directors of veterans affairs will also be notified by funeral directors and cemeteries within 96 hours of receiving the remains of a deceased service person.
This will help connect families with this local veterans’ resource which will be able to help them access benefits for which they might be eligible.

offers free virtual peer support for active-duty military, veterans, first responders and their immediate family members. Once registered, you can:
Join weekly virtual “Get Togethers”
Connect with fellow veterans and family members
Access wellness resources and community programming
There is no cost for eligible members.

Legislation we unanimously passed enacting stronger protections from deceptive telemarketing practices will take effect next month.
Under
Act 47 of 2026
, Pennsylvania’s telemarketing law will now cover modern forms of solicitation, including text messages, voicemails, ringless voicemails and robocalls. It also establishes stronger rules for when and how telemarketers can contact Pennsylvanians, including:
Prohibiting telemarketing calls before 9 a.m. and after 7 p.m. and on Sundays.
Requiring prior express written consent for most robocalls and telemarketing text messages.
Prohibiting telemarketers from falsely identifying themselves or using deceptive caller ID information, including spoofed numbers.
Requiring telemarketers to stop a solicitation when a consumer asks them to do so.
The legislation also prohibits the use of AI-generated messages to deceive consumers. The new law takes effect Oct. 19.

New Crosswalk on Brownsville Rd. in Memory of Isabella Shinn
Last Tuesday, we held a dedication ceremony on Brownsville Rd. in Lower Southampton and Bensalem townships to unveil pedestrian safety improvements in memory of Isabella Shinn, who was tragically killed walking home from work at Bruster’s Ice Cream almost four years ago.
I joined family and friends of the Shinn family, along with Rep. Hogan, Bensalem Township Mayor Joseph DiGirolamo, and local officials from Lower Southampton and Bensalem townships for the unveiling of dedications signs and a ribbon cutting at the new crosswalk.
After her passing, the Shinn family advocated for safety improvements to honor Isabella’s memory and to ensure the road was safer for all pedestrians. Rep. Tomlinson, Rep. Hogan, and I secured the funding for the project and worked with Pennsylvania Department of Transportation (PennDOT) and Bensalem and Lower Southampton townships for several years to make it happen.
Isabella was only 18 years old when she passed, was set to graduate from Archbishop Wood and was accepted to all the many colleges she applied to in Pennsylvania. She had a second-degree blackbelt, was a swim instructor and a Phillies fan.
It was a bittersweet day to finally see this come to fruition and provide some peace for the Shinn family. This crosswalk will carry Isabella’s name and her memory, but more importantly I hope it reminds drivers to slow down and pay attention.
The improvements include a new pedestrian crosswalk, pedestal-mounted rectangular rapid flashing beacons (RRFBs), new ADA-compliant curb ramps, new sidewalks and a dedication sign in memory of Isabella.
For more information about Isabella and the efforts her family is making to keep her memory alive.
DART’s 25th Anniversary and Grand Opening of Warminster Line
It was great to join the DART Committee and Bucks County Transport last Wednesday to celebrate the DART’s 25th anniversary and grand opening of their new DART East-Warminster line.
I was proud to present a citation to the DART for their anniversary and a check to Bucks County Transport for $550,000 in state funding from the Senate of PA that I helped secure to support the expansion of their Warminster line and continuation of their Warrington line.
DART, part of Bucks County Transport provides affordable, reliable transportation for residents traveling to appointments, shopping, work, and other essential stops. I will always advocate for public transit funding that is critical to our area.
William Penn Fire Company Awards Banquet
I attended William Penn Fire Company’s Banquet last Saturday, where members were celebrated for their years of dedicated service serving the community. I was honored to recognize a few of those members with citations from the Senate of Pennsylvania.
Congratulations to Chris Russel who was recognized as their Firefighter of the Year and to the following for their years of service:
Bryan Kohler—40 years
James Bampfield—35 years
Andy Conaway—30 years
Lara Horvath—10 years
Aaron Bradshaw—5 years
Jack Devine—5 years
Todd Dipopolo—5 years
First responders are routinely called upon to perform extraordinary acts which are often taken for granted despite the risks. Congratulations to the honorees and thank you to the entire department for your commitment and dedication to protecting our community.
Help Bag Hunger Day in Warminster

It was a true community effort and every donation accepted and every bag packed directly supports local feeding initiatives, including the vital work of the Warminster Food Bank, making a tangible difference for our neighbors facing food insecurity.
Medication Take Back Day is October 24
Medication Take Back Day is Saturday, October 24, 2026 from 10 am – 2 pm! This year’s Take Back event will feature 49 public collection sites throughout the county. Simply walk or drive up and drop in any unused, unneeded or expired medications for safe disposal.
In addition to prescription medications, law enforcement officers will be collecting over-the-counter and pet medications, vitamins, vaping products and more. Plus, select sites throughout the county will be collecting medications and sharps and distributing Narcan on October 24!

raw_text:

E-news Updates - September 25, 2026 - Senator Farry

In this Update:
Action Needed: Sign Our Petition for a Youth Activities Tax Credit
Out in the Community Last Weekend

Action Needed: Sign Our Petition for a Youth Activities Tax Credit
Are you a parent or guardian watching the cost of youth activities put a strain on your family’s budget? My colleagues and I have introduced legislation that would provide families with a tax credit of up to
$2,000 per child for eligible youth activities
and we need your help getting it moving in Harrisburg as we head back there next week.
Sign our petition today
.
Too often, good legislation can take years to become law. With enough support from families like yours, we can show our fellow lawmakers that Pennsylvania families want and need this tax credit—and help get it passed sooner. Read more about
Senate Bill 1441
and
House Bill 2753
.
Out in the Community Last Weekend
Last weekend was busy out in the community, starting with Friday night at Neshaminy High School’s football game for First Responder Night. Thank you to Neshaminy for recognizing the service and sacrifice of all our first responders. I was honored to stand alongside my fellow first responders and proud to serve our community every day.
The rest of the weekend was full of events, connecting with community members, while also making time for my family.
Rep. Tomlinson and I hosted a fall shredding event at Bensalem High School, I stopped by Penndel Borough’s 250th Anniversary Celebration, celebrated Orville Hutchins’ 100th birthday, joined the American Legion Riders Chapter 960 for their pig roast, and celebrated Bensalem AME Church’s 208th anniversary and retirement of their 100th Pastor, Reverend Lugenure M. Jones.
And in between it all, I was especially glad I was able to make time to watch my son’s soccer game.
Thank You All Who Made Our Senior Expo a Success
Hundreds of local seniors joined us on Thursday for our annual Senior Expo. It was great to see so many familiar faces—and some new faces too.
Thank you to all the vendors that joined us, helping make the event a success by sharing valuable resources and information with our attendees. Thank you to Northampton Valley Country Club for hosting us. Everything was wonderful as usual.
Making sure our seniors have access to the resources and support they need has always been priority. I will continue to champion efforts to make life affordable for our seniors. I authored legislation to freeze property taxes for seniors and fought to protect access to affordable prescription medications—preventing 10,000 from losing coverage, keeping 12,000 from facing higher costs, and helping more than 32,000 seniors access to lower prescription costs.
If you were unable to make the event but need assistance, please call or stop by our office.
Captain Walter H. Sigafoos POW/MIA Memorial Highway
I joined Rep. Marcell, Rep. Hogan, Congressman Fitzpatrick and the Sigafoos family on Friday, also National POW/MIA day, for a ceremony honoring U.S. Air Force Capt. Walter H. Sigafoos III and naming a portion of Second Street Pike in his memory.
On April 25, 1971, Captain Sigafoos disappeared after the F-4 Phantom he was serving aboard crashed in Laos near the Ho Chi Minh Trail. According to officials, Captain Sigafoos remains the only Bucks County service member still listed as missing in action from the Vietnam War.
Renaming this road in honor of Captain Sigafoos will ensure his legacy of sacrifice and service are woven into the daily lives of the community he called home, making sure his story is never forgotten.
Suicide Prevention Month Raises Awareness and Spreads Hope
Suicide Prevention Month is a time to raise awareness, spread hope and encourage discussion of a difficult topic.
Warning signs of suicide include:
Comments about suicide
Increased alcohol and drug use
Aggressive behavior
Withdrawal from friends and family
Dramatic mood swings
Impulsive or reckless behavior
The
National Alliance on Mental Illness
has more information about risk factors.
The
988 Lifeline
provides free and confidential support over call, text or chat for people in distress 24 hours a day, seven days a week. Empathetic, trained professionals provide prevention and crisis resources for you or someone you know.
Garrity Announces $1,000 Bonus for Families’ Education Savings
Pennsylvania Treasurer Stacy Garrity is giving families with qualified PA 529 College and Career Saving Program Guaranteed Savings Plan (GSP) accounts a $1,000 bonus contribution, enhancing education savings for about 107,000 Pennsylvania families.

raw_text:

In this Update:
Breast Cancer Awareness Month
State Funding for Vehicles in Lower Southampton Township
Safe2Say Something Tipline
My Bill to Expand EMS Transport Options Passes from Committee
Breast Cancer Awareness Month
October is Breast Cancer Awareness Month, a time to honor survivors, support those affected by breast cancer and raise awareness about the importance of prevention and early detection. The American Cancer Society recommends that women at average risk begin annual screening mammograms at age 40. When breast cancer is detected at its earliest stages, the 5-year survival rate is 99%.
That’s why I have partnered with Jefferson Health to offer a
Free Mobile Mammogram Event next Friday October 9 from 9am to 3pm at Warrington Fire Co. #1,
located at 2310 Freedoms Way. If interested, call our office to schedule your appointment. 215-638-1784. Ask for Ashley.
I have been a strong advocate for expanding access to breast cancer screening and diagnostic care. I authored legislation that eliminates out-of-pocket costs for diagnostic mammograms, breast MRIs and ultrasounds for Pennsylvanians insured under state law. No patient should have to delay potentially lifesaving care because of the cost of a diagnostic test.
The issue is deeply personal for me, as my wife’s experience with breast cancer reinforced for me how critical timely access to diagnostic imaging is for early detection and treatment.
State Funding for Vehicles in Lower Southampton Township
Rep. Hogan and I are proud to have helped secure over $1,000,000 through
Local Share Account (LSA)
funds from the Commonwealth Financing Authority for the purchase of new vehicles to be operated in Lower Southampton Township.
Lower Southampton Fire Company will use the $630,000 they were awarded to purchase a new fire truck to replace its 2007 Special Service apparatus with a Wildland Brush Truck. The current apparatus is 18 years old, exceeding NFPA’s 15-year replacement recommendation.
Lower Southampton Township will use the $461,207 they were awarded to purchase a new municipal vehicle fleet, including replacing three outdated police vehicles, a mini track loader, and a dump truck with updated models.
These investments will help strengthen emergency response capabilities and improve the township’s ability to maintain critical public infrastructure without unexpected interruptions.
Safe2Say Something Tipline
This week, a local resident took an important step to help keep their school community safe by reporting a threat through the Safe2Say Something tipline. The school district worked with local law enforcement to address the situation.
I commend this resident for speaking up and doing the right thing. This is a reminder that residents, including students, have a resource to anonymously report threats or concerning activity.
As the co-author of the legislation that established Safe2Say Something in Pennsylvania, I encourage students, parents, and educators to learn more about this valuable program because speaking up can save lives.
Since the program implementation in 2019, 1,000,000 students have made reports.
Learn more about Safe2SAySomething.
My Bill to Expand EMS Transport Options Passes out of Committee
A bill I sponsored to give emergency medical services (EMS) providers greater flexibility in transporting patients to appropriate receiving facilities advanced unanimously from the Senate Institutional Sustainability and Innovation Committee this week.
As chair of this committee, this legislation is important as it removes unnecessary barriers and gives our EMS professionals more options to continue providing patients with the care they need, including taking a patient having a mental health issue to a crisis center.
The legislation also would ensure EMS agencies are appropriately reimbursed when they provide emergency treatment and, when necessary, transport a patient to an authorized receiving facility.
Senate Bill 1403
now advances to the full Senate for consideration.

National Fire Prevention Week
It’s National Fire Prevention Week. “Charging into Fire Safety” is this year’s theme and The National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) is reminding residents of the following device charging safety tips.
Use the cord and charger that came with your device or one approved by the manufacturer.
Charge on a hard, flat surface like a table, desk, or bare floor.
Unplug your device when it is fully charged.
Charge large items like e-bikes, scooters, and power tools outside when possible. Do not block exits when charging.
Stop using your device if it feels very hot, starts to swell, smells strange, leaks, smokes, or makes popping or hissing sounds.
When on a plane, keep devices where you can see them while charging. Do not charge e-cigarettes or vapes on the plane. Tell a flight attendant if you notice a problem with your device.
Local Fire Companies are hosting open houses that will provide resourceful fire safety tips and fun family activities.

District to Announce Volunteer Relief Aid
Capitol Fountain Dyed Pink in Honor of Breast Cancer Awareness Month

Auditor General DeFoor in 6
th
District to Announce Volunteer Relief Aid
I was honored to have Pennsylvania Auditor General Tim DeFoor in the 6th District yesterday to announce more than $71 Million in Aid to Support Volunteer Firefighters.
You can watch full press conference here
.
Auditor General DeFoor presented The Firemen’s Relief Association of Warrington Township a check for $215,228.98 to support their volunteer firefighters that choose to risk their own lives protecting our communities. I am grateful to Warrington Fire Co. 1 for hosting the event and for all they do serving our community.
I authored legislation,
Act 91 of 2020
, to expand and enhance several fire and emergency medical services programs. The legislation addressed ongoing challenges within the first responder community, including allowing these relief funds to be used for expenditures directly related to recruitment and retention.
As a fire chief and active volunteer firefighter for 37 years, I know firsthand how important this funding is to ensure our volunteer fire companies are prepared with the proper resources to respond when emergencies happen.
Capitol Fountain Dyed Pink for Breast Cancer Awareness
I was proud to join my colleagues and friends from the Pennsylvania Breast Cancer Coalition at the State Capitol as we kicked off Breast Cancer Awareness Month by turning the East Wing Fountain pink. I proudly wear pink for all those we lost to breast cancer, the survivors and thrivers, especially my wife Kristen who endured a two-year journey with breast cancer and is now cancer free.
The event was a powerful reminder of the importance of early detection and how it saves lives. I have been a long-time strong advocate for access to affordable healthcare, authoring legislation to ensure cost isn’t a barrier for women being screened for breast cancer—an effort reinforced by my own family’s experience.
My Bill to Strengthen Employee Ownership Opportunities Passes Senate
My bill to help Pennsylvania businesses transition to employee ownership and preserve jobs within commonwealth communities was approved by the Senate this week.
Senate Bill 478
would establish the state Office of Employee Ownership within the Department of Community and Economic Development (DCED) and create an employee ownership advocate to lead efforts to promote employee ownership, provide education and outreach, and connect businesses with available resources. It would also establish an Employee Ownership Advisory Board to advise DCED and the General Assembly on policies and programs supporting employee-owned businesses.
Pennsylvania has thousands of small and family-owned businesses that are critical to our communities and local economies. As business owners consider retirement or other transitions, employee ownership can provide another path to keep those businesses operating, protecting good-paying jobs and giving employees an opportunity to have a stake in the companies where they work.
This legislation is about keeping businesses rooted in Pennsylvania and providing workers a greater opportunity to share in their success.
Senate Bill 478 has received bipartisan support and now heads to the House of Representatives for consideration.
I am pictured here at New Age Industries, an,100% employee-owned manufacturer in Southampton.
School Bus Driver Safety Bill Approved by Senate
Approximately 1.5 million children are transported on school buses every day in Pennsylvania, and the Senate approved legislation aimed at keeping reckless bus drivers from getting behind the wheel.
Senate Bill 1262
would increase penalties for school bus drivers who transport children while under the influence of alcohol, a controlled substance or a dangerous combination of both.
Read more about this school bus safety measure
.
The latest Senate action follows passage last year of
Senate Bill 65
, which would increase the required stopping distance for drivers approaching from the opposite direction when a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing. Both bills await passage in the House of Representatives.
Senate Passes Bill to Establish Animal Abuser Registry
The Senate approved
Senate Bill 1311
, known as Aimee’s Law, to help prevent convicted abusers from obtaining more animals by establishing a statewide animal abuser registry. The bill was sent to the House of Representatives for consideration.

In this Update:
Wishing You a Happy and Healthy New Year
2025 Review: Improving Pennsylvania Health Care
PA Treasury Mails Nearly 100,000 Money Match Checks
PA State Police Chaplaincy Program Accepting Applications
Wishing You a Happy and Healthy New Year
As we turn the calendar page on another eventful year, I want to wish you and your family a happy and healthy 2026.
May the new year bring you joy and success, shared with those you love.
2025 Review: Improving Pennsylvania Health Care
Healthy and safe communities are one of my top priorities. The Senate passed several measures in 2025 aimed at improving health care across Pennsylvania. Legislation I authored, Senate Bill 88, now Act 52 of 2025,
expands no-cost breast cancer screenings
, marking a major advancement in cancer care and early detection efforts,
Other legislation of note included bills
saving lives
from
overdoses
and
preserving prescription drug coverage
for seniors. The Senate also acted to
alleviate staffing shortages
in
long-term care facilities
, expand access to
high-quality maternity services
, and more.
As we enter the second year of the 2025-26 legislative session, I’ll continue working to improve access to affordable, quality health care. Read more about health care legislation and other important bills
here
.
PA Treasury Mails Nearly 100,000 Money Match Checks
Check your mailboxes, because the Pennsylvania Treasury Department recently mailed nearly 100,000
Pennsylvania Money Match
checks totaling more than $22 million. Treasurer Stacy Garrity urges those who receive a check to cash or deposit it immediately – this is a real program, and this money belongs to Pennsylvanians.
Money Match, a law that went into effect in 2025, allows the Pennsylvania Treasury to return single-owner unclaimed property valued at $500 or less automatically without the need to search or file a claim. Money Match successfully returned $50 million in its first year and will continue issuing checks quarterly.
More than one in 10 Pennsylvanians is owed some of the over $5 billion of unclaimed property in Treasury’s care. The average value of a claim is $1,000. Visit
patreasury.gov/unclaimed-property
to start searching.
I recently introduced legislation,
Senate Bill 844
, to increase the current limit of $500 to $10,000 to allow more Pennsylvanians to have the opportunity to get their property and money back.
PA State Police Chaplaincy Program Accepting Applications
The Pennsylvania State Police (PSP) is accepting applications from Pennsylvanians who want to volunteer as PSP chaplains.
The positions are open to licensed or ordained clergy interested in providing spiritual support to state troopers. Interested residents are encouraged to apply by Jan. 1, 2026. Contact
RA-SPMAP@pa.gov
for details and applications.

Happy Holidays!
I offer you my warm wishes for a very Merry Christmas filled with joy and laughter. May you and your family enjoy a holiday season that is marked by joy and love.
My district office hours may be limited due to the holidays. Please call ahead, 215-638-1784, to be sure my office is open.

I was honored to attend the ceremony for Rick Hazelett’s promotion to Lieutenant of the Buckingham Police Department last week. Rick’s dedication to public service — including his many years as a local volunteer firefighter, speaks volumes about his commitment to our community.
Also, congratulations to the three new Buckingham PD police officers sworn in last week. Thank you all for choosing to serve and protect.
